topic: STARTING OVER: finding your first number, what's coming in, by circling the repeating deposits on last month's checking statement in about 20 minutes
pillar: STARTING OVER: the feelings and the small first moves (the 2 A.M. math, 'where did the money go, not why', permission to go slowly).
caption:
If starting over feels like too much, start with the money that comes in.
Grab last month's checking statement and look only at the deposits.
Write each one down, circle the ones you expect again, and add those up.
That's your first number. Unsure lines get a question mark, and that's fine.
Save this for a quiet morning when you have twenty minutes ☕

slides.title: Start with the money that comes in
slides.subtitle: A 20-minute look at one statement

slides.title: You can begin with the gentlest number
slides.body: Of the Three Numbers, what's coming in is often the shortest list. One statement and twenty minutes is plenty. You can go slowly with this.

slides.title: Set yourself up first
items: Last month's checking statement, paper or in the app
A pen and one blank page
Your phone or laptop, if the statement lives there

slides.title: Find your first number
items: Look only at the deposits column. Skip the rest for today.
Write each deposit on its own line, with the date.
Next to each one, write where it came from.
Circle the ones you expect to see again next month.
Add up the circled ones. That's your first number.

slides.title: What the page might look like
slides.body: Example with made-up numbers: two paychecks of 1,400 and 300 from a side job. Circled total, 3,100. A one-time refund gets written down but stays uncircled.

slides.title: Put a question mark and keep going
slides.body: Support payments or money that might change can get a question mark. A licensed professional can help with the details. Today you only write it down.

slides.title: Stop when the twenty minutes are up
slides.body: One statement is the whole step. The other two numbers can wait for another day. Put the page somewhere you will see it this week.

slides.title: Save this for a quiet morning
slides.body: The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet has a spot for this number and the other two. It's one page, free in my Stan store, link in bio. Day one counts.
